name: ZoRoCo Packaging - Free From Plant
old_description: Founded and fueled by the spirit of family, ZoRoCo Packaging offers experience, passion, and integrity.
about:
ZoRoCo Packaging was founded in 2007 in Caldwell, Idaho, by Cordy and Kim Rost. The couple, formerly of Southern California—Cordy an aerospace engineer with corporate finance experience, Kim a structural engineer—relocated to Kim's home state to raise their family. They acquired a small frozen food packaging business called IdaCold, and with the involvement of Kim's father, food industry executive Marc Ikebasu, began building a contract manufacturing operation. The company name derives from their children's names: Zoe, Ronin, and Cole.

Today ZoRoCo operates three manufacturing facilities on a campus about 30 minutes southwest of Boise, employing over 400 people. The plants hold GFSI BRCGS A+ to AA ratings and specialize in frozen and allergen-free food contract manufacturing and co-packing. Capabilities include IQF processing of vegetables, fruits, and plant-based products; blending, enrobing, and chopping; vertical form-fill-seal bagging from 4 ounces to 6 pounds; tray and carton shrink wrapping; lidded tubs and peel-and-go cups; bulk packaging up to 60 pounds; and high-care ready-to-eat production in 20,000 square feet of expanded space added in 2019. A USDA-approved cold storage facility provides 4,500 temperature-controlled pallet positions with cross-docking, container loading, and export documentation services.

The company serves food brands and entrepreneurs across the frozen, gluten-free, allergen-free, and plant-based segments. Clients range from startups launching vegan cheese and butter spreads to established brands needing co-packing for IQF produce, ready-to-eat meals, and variety packs. ZoRoCo's dedicated gluten-free plant (built 2022) and Big 9 allergen-free capabilities allow it to handle sensitive formulations without cross-contamination risk.

ZoRoCo positions itself as a non-competitor—it markets no brands of its own—and emphasizes transparency through live client access to production, inventory, and shipping data. The founders cite an entrepreneurial mentality, precision execution, and certification and claims management as core differentiators, aiming to protect clients' intellectual property while scaling capacity alongside their growth.

name: Zoila's Sample Room Inc
old_description: Whether you want to start developing your designs or you’re ready to jump into production, Zoila’s Sample Room partners with designers and fashion brands to transform beautiful ideas into custom garments. We work closely with our clients to capture their concepts and ideas, and create one of a kind designs.
about:
Zoila's Sample Room Inc. operates in New York City's Garment Center, founded in 2005 by Zoila Cruz. Cruz began sewing in her hometown in Ecuador before moving to New York, where she worked for designers such as Morgane Le Fay, Miguelina, Libertine, and Thakoon. She launched her own sample room in 2005, building a reputation for turning sketches into finished garments.

The shop provides end‑to‑end pattern and sample development, including draping, fitting, alterations, and custom orders. It handles production runs ranging from 13 to 200 pieces and works with a broad spectrum of fabrics — knits, silk chiffon, jersey, netting, denim, wool, leather, fur, sequins, lace, and delicate materials that require extra care.

Clients include established New York labels and emerging designers from Miami, Los Angeles, Boston, Washington DC, and upstate New York. Past collaborators include Morgane Le Fay, Miguelina, Libertine, and Thakoon, while testimonials cite brands led by Jonathan Simkhai, Camilla Staerk, and others who have used the shop for runway samples, sales‑order production, and made‑to‑measure red‑carpet and wedding gowns.

The company emphasizes Cruz’s three decades of pattern‑making experience and her ability to guide designers from initial sketch to model‑ready garments, often coordinating remotely via Instagram, email, video, and phone. In 2020 the CFDA featured her in its LatinX Series, highlighting her role in bringing new designers’ visions to life.

The company distributes a broad range of products including copper wire, magnet wire, wire and cable, electrical insulation materials such as mica, flexible and rigid insulation, lacing and banding, adhesives and sealants, pressure-sensitive tape, terminals and connectors, as well as motors, motor parts, shop equipment, and test equipment. It serves electrical OEMs and motor repair shops across the Midwest.

Primary customers are electrical original equipment manufacturers and motor repair facilities, with a focus on apparatus repair and electrical OEM sites in the Midwestern United States. The company also supplies materials for electrical insulation applications in industrial and commercial settings.

Alternative Wire & Cable states its mission is to be the service and solutions provider for electrical insulation materials to apparatus repair and electrical OEM sites in the Midwestern United States, emphasizing customer priority and regional expertise.

name: boston semi equipment
old_description: Partnership with our customers to deliver high-performance electronics test handling equipment and service solutions for semiconductor device testing. Motivated by the growing need for flexible IC test solutions, Boston Semi Equipment (BSE) thrives on solving complex technology problems with production-ready electronic test handling equipment built for the long haul.
about:
Boston Semi Equipment (BSE) is based in Littleton, Massachusetts. The company was founded to address the growing need for flexible IC test solutions, thriving on solving complex technology problems with production-ready electronic test handling equipment built for the long haul.

BSE designs and manufactures advanced test handlers, including the Zeus series of gravity handlers and the Panacea series of pick-and-place handlers, with variants for tri-temperature, MEMS, high-voltage, and high-accuracy applications. Beyond hardware, the company provides a full suite of services: installation, warranty, training, parts replacement, field service, relocation, calibration, and repair of legacy ATE boards and systems. Repair work is performed at ISO-certified facilities in Thailand and the Philippines, supported by regional logistics centers that maintain extensive parts inventories.

The company serves semiconductor device testing customers across automotive, electrification (wide-bandgap semiconductors), collaborative technology (connectivity and smart devices), aerospace, medical (MEMS), and AI and big data markets. BSE also supports the global installed base of legacy ATE equipment and test cells long after original manufacturers phase them out.

BSE emphasizes close customer partnerships as its core differentiator, stating that its biggest accomplishments result from collaborations that push the edges of technology and deliver exceptional value for today and tomorrow. The business was motivated by the need for flexible, production-ready test handling equipment that endures.

about:
hg medical USA operates as the U.S. subsidiary of hg medical GmbH, headquartered in Holland, Michigan, with a production facility in Huntington, West Virginia. The company was established after Wright Medical acquired the DARCO implant division, and later became majority-owned by Nord Holding.

The company manufactures orthopedic implants for bone surgery, processing approved raw materials such as titanium, stainless steel, and PEEK on modern machining centers at its sites in Raisting, Germany, and Huntington, West Virginia. Its U.S. facility has added automated milling capabilities. Both locations run independent quality management systems certified to ISO 13485 and comply with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, having undergone full FDA audits.

hg medical serves original equipment manufacturers in the orthopedic market, ranging from global market leaders to emerging startups. Its implants are used in bone surgery procedures worldwide, and the company emphasizes traceability and regulatory compliance for medical device OEMs.

The company states that its differentiator lies in operating completely independent, ISO 13485-certified quality systems at each production site, combined with full FDA audit experience and a commitment to using only approved materials. Management describes its standard as "Best in Class" and invites customer audits to demonstrate quality firsthand.

name: iSolar
old_description: Since 2020 we’ve helped income-qualified Minnesotans get solar at little-to-no cost through Xcel’s Solar*Rewards Income-Qualified program — wiping out electric bills for families who need it most.
about:
iSolar is based in St. Paul Park, Minnesota, and was co-founded in 2019 by master electrician John Ihle and his nephew Ryan Ihle. The company is family-owned and veteran-owned, with roots in the Minnesota electrical trade dating back to 1977 and renewable-energy work since the 1980s — experience the firm says few other solar installers in the state can match.

iSolar provides full-service solar, storage, and electrical work for homes, farms, and businesses across Minnesota. Its services cover residential solar, commercial and agricultural solar, battery backup, EV charger installation, electrical panel upgrades, wiring, standby generators, and solar array detach-and-reset for roofing projects. The company uses its own crew for installations, completing most residential jobs in one to two days under master electrician license EA761814. It holds manufacturer certifications for major brands including Enphase, SolarEdge, Tesla Powerwall, Generac, and Kohler, and backs every system with a 30-year insurance-backed warranty through Solar Insure plus a 20-year battery warranty.

The installer serves Minnesota homeowners, farmers, businesses, schools, and public entities. Since 2020 it has helped income-qualified families access solar at little-to-no cost through Xcel Energy's Solar*Rewards Income-Qualified program. Since 2019 it has assisted farmers with projects funded partly by USDA REAP grants. Public-sector work includes solar on school buildings and a 100 kW AC array at Edina City Hall. iSolar has also been selected as a co-op installer by Solar United Neighbors for 2022, 2023, and 2024.

The company says it was started to do solar "the right way" for neighbors — emphasizing a single local crew from start to finish with no subcontractor shuffle, custom solutions from experienced designers, honest fair pricing, and a 30-year warranty. Its family-owned, veteran-owned structure and deep Minnesota roots are presented as reasons customers can trust the firm for the long term.

name: interplas® (International Plastics)
old_description: interplas® (International Plastics®) is a wholesale supplier and manufacturer of flexible packaging and plastic bags. We stock 9,000+ items:
about:
International Plastics, operating as interplas®, is headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina. The company was founded in 1964 by J.R. McClure, who borrowed $500 from his mother to start producing polyethylene bags for the region's textile mills. His wife, Frances, joined him in building the business one customer at a time. The company remains family-owned, with the second generation now helping set strategic direction.

The firm manufactures, imports, and wholesale supplies flexible packaging and plastic bags, stocking more than 9,000 items across 250-plus categories. Its product range includes poly bags, reclosable ziplock bags, trash bags and liners, poly tubing and film, stretch and shrink film, and shipping supplies. Custom printing, custom sizing, and in-house artwork services (with two hours of free art time per order) are offered through four purchasing paths: stock packaging with same-day shipping, bulk pallet and truckload orders, custom printed packaging, and just-in-time inventory programs. All orders run through an ISO 9001 certified quality system, and the company operates from ten stocking locations nationwide.

Interplas serves food service, healthcare, retail and apparel, security, moving and storage, warehouse and industrial, and electronics and ESD markets. Its customer base includes businesses, resellers, and distributors who buy at wholesale, factory-direct pricing.

The company traces its differentiation to its founding principle that "doing right by people is good business." It emphasizes a people-first culture, audited processes, same-day shipping on stock orders, a lowest-price guarantee, and a 100% satisfaction guarantee.

name: moisture sensors, dew point sensors
old_description: The ZDC Tech’s patented hybrid dielectric sensors are the world’s most advanced humidity/dew point sensors manufactured using the latest nanotechnology, featuring with long-term stability, fast response, and durability in extremely high/low humidity levels. It can be recovered even after exposure to liquid water! It can monitor both dew point and temperature with a temperature sensor provided. Proper use of the meter can provide lifelong reliability without recalibration. The superior performance of the sensor makes it an ideal choice for many industrial applications.
about:
ZDC Tech is based in Lexington, Kentucky. The company traces its roots to 2011 when Advanced Semiconductor Processing Technology (ASPT) was established to commercialize a novel humidity sensor invented by Dr. David Chen, a professor of electrical engineering at the University of Kentucky. ZDC Tech continues that research and development lineage today.

The company designs and manufactures dew point transmitters (models E80 and E100) and portable dew point meters, all built on its patented hybrid dielectric sensor platform produced with nanotechnology methods. It also operates a dew point sensor calibration service. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not disclosed.

ZDC Tech serves industrial customers needing humidity and dew point measurement, though specific sectors are not named in its public materials.

The company emphasizes that its sensors offer long-term stability, fast response, and durability across extreme humidity levels, can recover after liquid water exposure, and provide lifelong reliability without recalibration. A newer generation of sensors is said to respond five times faster than the previous version.
